title: Need tips managing AI Usage Limits in Unity 6 Project
author: Psychological-Arm42
selftext:
I’ve been building a game in unity 6, using the 20$ claude plan, with opus 5.5 High.

I’ve started to hit my claude weekly limits faster, as my   
game gets bigger. Just Last week I exhausted my weekly limit in 3 days, working about 4-5 hrs each.

So I decided to buy the 20$ gpt codex as well, since I’ve heard it provides more usage limits than claude. Now I have both codex and claude, working on the same project.

Claude : Reads the project design graph (gains context, \~50K tokens right now), orchestrates, plans the chrrent task, then hands out appropriate amount work to codex. so basically claude does the heavy-lifting, descision making, and planning, wheras codex does the implenetation of the set instructions given by claude.

Any tips which could help improve token use? Or a more efficient method to use both subscriptions?

(I have tried using codex individually, without orchestrated tasks from claude: It fails miserably when trying to execute tasks on its own)

comments.author: Slow-Win8148
comments.body: Don’t use opus 5.5 high on 20$ sub use medium its enough and your usage will reduce a bit. Or buy 100$ claude sub. Codex is not good at games as much as claude.

replies.author: because-potato
replies.body: What is your backing for this? I’ve published 2 phenomenal games using only codex. I’ve used Claude and codex side by side and their performance is almost identical, Claude is just more nervous

replies.author: Psychological-Arm42
replies.body: I thought so, I now regret buying codex. I should have bought another 20$ subscription of claude on a different account. 100$ I think is overkill though

comments.author: xThe_Great_Bambino
comments.body: a long session costs more per turn than a short one. Running /clear when you switch tasks means you stop paying to resend old and unrelated context, which can noticeably cut token usage

replies.author: Psychological-Arm42
replies.body: I'm already doing this. I've split my game into \~8 development phases, and each phase into \~5-6 milestones (claude does that) and I open a new chat after each milestone. On average, total context stays below 200K.

comments.author: TheBigQuestion354
comments.body: don't know what kind of game you are building but I'd highly recommend switching to Godot, way better for AI game development. Also it's going to be really tough to build something on the cheap plans, and like the other guy said Claude is better at coding. GPT isn't all bad but Astra is the only model I use.

replies.author: Psychological-Arm42
replies.body: When I first saw opus 5.5 and decided to jump into game dev, I thought the 20$ plan would suffice. I'm just now realizing it's nowhere near enough. But since it's my first game, and I'm mostly busy with college stuff and only get about 3-4 hours a day I'll try to finish it using the 20$ plans as best as I can. Still a somewhat ambitious project though.

comments.author: Suspicious-Engineer7
comments.body: refactor and clean up the context as much as you can. limit how much it has to look at with each task. If it's working on the inventory system, it shouldn't need to read your whole project.

comments.author: Old-Wolverine-4134
comments.body: 20$ and you managed to get 3 days? It's actually a lot. Even with $200 i've hit weekly limit many times in 3-4 days.

replies.author: Psychological-Arm42
replies.body: I've tried to optimize as much as I can, and I only built about 10% of the game in those 3 days so not that much usage

comments.author: Hot-Middle7260
comments.body: tell me you’re delusional without telling me you’re delusional? $20 and you’re hoping to gamedev with opus? Brother I have two Claude $200 sub and 1 Codex $500 sub and I need more.

replies.author: Psychological-Arm42
replies.body: I'm not making any hotshot 3D AAA game though. I'm just making a top-down RPG type game like hades 2.

replies.author: Opposite_Koala2299
replies.body:
If this is your goal, I'd honestly just ask AI to walk you through the steps of creation for a good chunk to save on token usage. 

Godot is FANTASTIC for 2d games and learning hands on whilst using AI to help. 

Give it a shot! I think it'll be interesting.

replies.author: Hot-Middle7260
replies.body: Not OP but I second this suggestion. OP, use opus to teach you how to make games. especially if you’re doing small top down rpg theres really no reason for you to offload the work other than being lazy. Dont be lazy OP

comments.author: Legal_Steak_4609
comments.body: For some cases it's better to create plans with gpt and review with claude. Same with code: implement with gpt > review with claude -> update with gpt.

comments.author: Harlan_42
comments.body:
I get the same thing...and hid documentation was burying me.  Being I am sitting right there to test; I specifically have to tell him to let me help.  I finally added to my [claude.md](http://claude.md) that point and if I see him going for Playwright...I interrupt.  So now he switched to harnesses, more of a digital simulation of my game, and spins his wheels doing theses test.  I have 5 tracks so there is a time and place, but not while I am developing features, after I think I am done.  Finally, I told him that he keeps doing harnesses and I keep finding problems, but I got to keep a close I on him.  I am working on a new app to help organize and work on games so follow me if you want.

Tip: use a screen recorder with video editor to isolate frames and use the screen as reference.  Create a debug screen that can capture info to convey back to Claude, specifics matter.

comments.author: Sad-Bus4090
comments.body:
Use a AI agent framework that delegates tasks between paid flagship models like opus/astra and a locally ran model like Qwen/Deepseek...etc

opus and astra are super happy to create project directories an setup basic scenes for GODOT or Unity and take all your usage credits along with them. But these small tasks can be delegated to local models instead. Qwen/Deepseek can handle setting up a project, creating player movement scripts, creating weapon and inventory scripts...etc. While Opus/Astra focus on reviewing, editing and refining. 

This workflow is something i've started myself with generally good results, its a bit slower, granted, but i've saved a significant about of usage credits in most projects. I'd say about 70% of my overall tokens are from my local coding agent.

replies.author: Psychological-Arm42
replies.body: Interesting. which local model should I use? qwen or deepseek? I have 16GB total ram, rtx 4060 Laptop GPU and ryzen 7 7840HS processor.

replies.author: Sad-Bus4090
replies.body:
You're gonna be limited to older models unfortunately so you won't get as good results I expect, but: 

Qwen3 8B or DeepSeek-R1 8B

I should have mentioned that I have a 5070 and 64GB of RAM so I'm using Qwen3-Coder 30B.

Still its worth benchmarking your results, and saved usage is worth it. Good luck!

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body: You don't even need local. Simply using something like GLM Flash for mundane tasks will save a lot of money.

comments.author: Kupke
comments.body: i wouldnt say i would trust any llm with anything but ive had pretty good experiences letting codex pickup some tasks when claude is at usage limit, but i have a central repo, working folders and branches set up in orca

comments.author: butchiebags
comments.body: If you haven’t already, try sonnet 5.5 and maybe even haiku 5.5 with subtasks.  For a local model, I’d recommend a small 3 bit quant of qwen 3.8 27b. You can probably fit just enough in your 16GB vram with 64k context window.  Ask Claude to set it up for you, you can setup llama.cpp and run it with pi coding agent, then no more token limits.  The quality is going to be limited but very useable.  I use this exact model to find specific variables and make tweaks in my code base all the time, it’s small enough I can run it next to my game while I’m playing it (I’m on a 32 GB 5090). I see people recommending older models, but the newer ones at low quant I think are better.

comments.author: Count_JohnnyJ
comments.body: Only use high or above for creating PLANS. Once the smart AI writes the assignment plan, give it to a low/light chat to do the actual work. You will save an extraordinary amount of usage, and the light model is completely capable of following all of the instructions in the assignment. If after a few iterations things aren't where you want them, create a focused list of things you want fixed, bump it up to medium, and give it one attempt. It'll probably knock it out.

comments.author: Whole-Description646
comments.body:
those are rookie numbers. I exhaust my 20x max in 2 days on my game. 

Nothing to do with the game getting bigger and everything to do with building skills and automations that let the agents do more faster so I hit the limit sooner. 

It's nice and sucks at the same time but now I have 4 days to really lock in what changes to make and then there are the human pieces like manually polishing models , rigs, sound, etc. so it actually works well
